claims.statement: For every diagonal form in the original independent coordinates with at least three coefficients of magnitude >=1, Q(X) has a bounded uniformly continuous density with ||p_Q||_infinity<=pi.

dependencies.scope: same-sign diagonal pair has bounded density <=pi

claims.statement: For independent Y1,Y2,Y3 with densities <=1 and any symmetric invertible 3x3 B with sigma_min(B)=kappa, every affine quadratic Y^T B Y+2b^T Y+c has an absolutely continuous law with density norm <=(2*pi+3*sqrt(3))/kappa.
If A has a principal coordinate 3x3 block with sigma_min>=kappa, then ||p_{X^TAX}||_infinity <=(2*pi+3*sqrt(3))/kappa, allowing arbitrary cross-couplings to conditioned coordinates.

For infinitely many n there are rank-three orthogonal projections A with three eigenvalues exactly1 such that every 3x3 principal coordinate block has sigma_min<=3/n, while sum_{|I|=3} det(A_II)=1. Hence selecting one coordinate triple cannot be dimension-free.

Convert the aggregate determinant/minor resource of delocalized three-dimensional spectral directions into P(X^TAX in J)<=C|J| without selecting one principal triple. Under the fleet03/B15 product-set reduction this is equivalently a shell-volume bound for Cartesian products of unit-measure measurable sets.

For the fully rotated target, interval domination gives an L-infinity density but not automatically a continuous representative. The stronger continuity assertion remains separate; this run proves it only on the full diagonal branch.

partner_result_applied.use: Its exact bathtub reduction converts the remaining aggregate-minor target into the geometric shell-volume statement for products E_1 x ... x E_n with |E_i|=1. The principal-triple theorem proves that geometric statement whenever one 3x3 principal block has uniform singular gap; the flat projector shows the partner reduction's first genuinely delocalized case cannot be solved by selecting one triple.
